newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals slide to fresh two month lows.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals slide to fresh two month lows.

text.p: New York precious metals prices slid to fresh two month lows Thursday before some shortcovering helped provide some support near the close.
"There's a dearth of investor demand, and industrial usage has not yet picked up after the usual summer lull," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"Renewed talk about IMF gold sales may be disconcerting to retail investors, but the plan has been discounted into prices by the trade for months," he said.
"The U.S. economy and equity markets are still ticking along nicely so there's little demand for safe haven gold."
COMEX December gold ended down 80 cents an ounce at $385.80, after seeing a three year low for the December contract at $384.60.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $382.45/382.95, compared to the London afternoon fix at $382.10, which was the lowest fix since July 9 this year.
COMEX December silver ended down 8.0 cents at $5.060, after seeing a two month low for the contract at $5.030.
Both gold and silver have drifted lower in the past three weeks, as fund selling and weak industrial demand brought an end to the July/August rally, analysts said.
